narrative.overview:
This is a guide written by and for people who now live partly in a terminal. The visual system fuses two things the product itself is about: a command-line identity (the ❯ brand glyph, literal monospace command syntax, a mini terminal window in the hero) and the three-rung ladder — Prompt → Skill → Subagent — the whole guide teaches. The tier ramp isn't decorative color variety; it's the one idea made visible, so the deepening green progression (--t1 → --t2 → --t3) must always track that specific meaning wherever it appears, never be reused as generic accent color. Green is the system's committed hue — the most literal color a terminal has (phosphor CRT green, git diff green) — not an arbitrary brand pick.

The feel is precise and unshowy: a cool, neutral gray-green paper (never cream, never beige, never terracotta, anywhere — a deliberate exclusion) carries small, confident type moves. Cards and rungs sit gently, permanently lifted off the paper. Every corner in the real UI is sharp — flat 0px radius, no exceptions. Borders are a deliberate 2px, not a hairline: components read as workmanlike and precise but not timid. One card per page — the single most important next step — inverts to solid ink with white text, spending real contrast exactly once rather than scattering it.

This is the third pass on the same instinct. The first removed a decorative hero grid, colored border-left accents, kicker/eyebrow labels, and bounce easing. The second flattened every rounded corner to 0px and swapped the display face from Bricolage Grotesque to the severer Archivo. This third pass replaced the violet/indigo tier ramp with a deepening terminal-green ramp (the most literal color a terminal has), shifted the paper from a warm off-white toward a cool neutral gray-green (explicitly excluding cream/beige/terracotta), thickened every primary card's border to a bold 2px, pushed the hero display type bigger and tighter, and inverted the single most important card per page to solid ink for real contrast.

A fourth pass fixed a layout bug where prose sections combined a page-centering container with a narrower reading-width cap on the same element, so the capped column re-centered itself inside the already-centered page — body copy started further right than the hero and nav above it. The reading-width cap (`.measure`) no longer self-centers; it left-aligns at the same edge as everything else, widened slightly (72ch → 75ch), and multi-column content (compare panels, card grids) was pulled out to the full page width instead of being squeezed narrow. The same pass raised body-scale type across the board (body 16.5px → 17.5px, nav links 11.5px → 12.5px, and roughly 40 other reading-scale sizes) for readability, while leaving code/terminal blocks alone.

Confirmed rejection: this system explicitly does not chase generic "AI-product" visual habits — no glossy gradient hero, no purple-on-white SaaS default, no stock illustration, no kicker-plus-headline template, no colored side-accent cards, no bounce easing, no soft-rounded default-app-icon geometry, no trendy variable-grotesque display face, no cream/beige/terracotta surface anywhere.
keyCharacteristics: Cool neutral gray-green paper (never cream, beige, or terracotta) with a bright near-white card surface for content
A deepening green tier ramp that always means Prompt→Skill→Subagent, carried by badges and tinted backgrounds — never a border accent, never a generic accent
Terminal/CLI vocabulary throughout: the ❯ glyph, monospace command chips, a dark terminal window
Ambient, always-on soft shadows — material lift at rest, not a hover reward
Sharp corners everywhere — 0px radius, no exceptions; the only curves are true circles (terminal window dots)
Bold 2px borders on every primary card-like surface — a deliberate, visible rule, not a hairline
One inverted solid-ink card per page marks the single most important next action — real contrast, spent once
Archivo display face at a bigger, tighter scale (up to 88px, -0.04em tracking) — severe and industrial, not a trendy variable-grotesque AI-marketing default
Every hero h1 leads its page directly, no kicker or eyebrow above it
Motion decelerates smoothly (exponential ease-out); nothing overshoots or springs
Reading-width prose is capped at 75ch but left-aligned, not centered — it starts at the same edge as the hero and full-width card grids
Body-scale type reads larger throughout (body 17.5px, nav 12.5px) for readability; code/terminal blocks keep their original size

rules.name: The Ladder-Only Rule
rules.body: The three tier colors (Prompt Green, Skill Green, Subagent Pine) and their soft/line tints exist to encode which rung of Prompt → Skill → Subagent a piece of UI refers to. Never repurpose them as a generic fourth or fifth accent color.

rules.name: The Soft/Line Rule
rules.body: Every accent color ships as a triplet: solid for fills, -soft for background wash, -line for border. Never place a solid accent directly on Paper without its matching tints doing the transition. Prompt Green additionally needs its -ink variant anywhere it carries text.

rules.name: The No-Cream Rule
rules.body: Cream, beige, and terracotta are excluded from this palette entirely — a confirmed rejection, not a default avoided by chance. Any warm neutral shifts cool/gray-green first, never toward tan or ivory.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Chrome Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for structural/interface text — never for headlines or body prose. If something is set in mono, it is labeling or instructing, not narrating.

rules.name: The Always-Lifted Rule
rules.body: Cards and rungs are never flat at rest. If a new component needs to feel calmer than the default card, reduce padding — don't remove the shadow or thin the border.

rules.name: The Badge-Not-Border Rule
rules.body: Category and tier meaning live in a colored number badge, a tinted background, or a colored heading — never in a border accent color. A colored border-left or border-top on a card, rung, callout, day block, or compare panel is a rejected pattern here.

rules.name: The Sharp-Corner Rule
rules.body: Every surface in the real UI is 0px radius. The only curves are true circles standing in for a real round object. A rounded rectangle anywhere in the real chrome is a regression, not a style choice.

rules.name: The One Inversion Rule
rules.body: Solid-ink, white-text card treatment is spent on exactly one card per page — the single most important next step. Using it more than once per page dilutes it into decoration.

rules.name: The Left-Align Rule
rules.body: The reading-width measure cap (75ch) never self-centers. It left-aligns at the same edge as the full-width hero and card grids around it. Multi-column content (compare panels, card grids) stays at full page width instead of being squeezed into the reading measure.

dos: Do keep the tier ramp (Prompt Green / Skill Green / Subagent Pine) meaning-locked to the three rungs; never introduce a fourth 'tier-like' color.
Do pair every accent color with its own -soft background and -line border tint rather than placing a solid accent directly on Paper.
Do set structural/interface text (nav, tags, code, terminal, callout/card labels) in JetBrains Mono, uppercase, widely tracked where it's a label.
Do give every primary card-like surface an ambient shadow at rest, sharp corners, and a bold 2px border.
Do carry category/tier meaning with a colored number badge, a tinted background, or a colored heading — never a border accent.
Do let every hero h1 lead the page directly, with the lede paragraph doing any framing a label might otherwise carry.
Do keep every corner sharp — 0px radius across the entire real UI.
Do use prompt-green-ink, never raw Prompt Green, anywhere that color carries text.
Do spend the one inverted solid-ink card on exactly one thing per page.
donts: Don't use cream, beige, or terracotta anywhere in this system — not the background, not a tint, not an accent.
Don't reach for a generic purple-on-white 'AI SaaS' gradient hero, glossy CTA, or stock illustration — green in this system is load-bearing ladder meaning, not category decoration.
Don't make elevation hover-only. Shadows here are ambient/material; hover deepens an existing shadow, it doesn't create one from flat.
Don't set headline or body prose in JetBrains Mono — mono means interface chrome, not narration.
Don't round any corner in the real UI — the radius scale is 0px across the board.
Don't thin a primary card's border below 2px — reserve 1px for secondary/nested elements only.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above an h1/h2 headline — removed sitewide as a recognizable AI-generated-UI tell.
Don't add a colored border-left/border-top accent to a card, rung, callout, day block, or compare panel — removed sitewide.
Don't draw a decorative hairline grid or line-field behind a hero — removed.
Don't use overshoot/bounce easing — replaced sitewide with a smooth exponential ease-out (cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)).
Don't use Ink, Faint (--ink-3) for real reader-facing text on the actual guide pages — it fails WCAG AA; reserved for the showcase.html demo product's palette.
Don't reach for Bricolage Grotesque, Space Grotesk, Syne, or another trendy variable-grotesque display face — replaced with Archivo.
Don't use raw Prompt Green as text color on a light surface — it fails contrast at ~2:1; use prompt-green-ink instead.
